Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: runtime animated enemy sprite sheet for a top-down anime pixel RPG, not concept illustration. Image 1 is a STYLE REFERENCE for dark outlines, pixel clusters and vivid shading, NOT a request to draw a slime. Primary request: A forest moss scarab: emerald segmented shell, angular moss plates, six articulated black-green legs, sharp small mandibles, fierce amber eyes. A natural armored forest monster, not a smiling pet..
Art direction: authentic hand-pixelled JRPG anime monster, expressive threatening combat silhouette, not a plush toy or big-headed kawaii mascot. Crisp staircase contours, visible square pixel clusters, deliberately limited palette of 16-24 colors, hard cel shading in 4-5 tones, sharp highlights. Render as if the monster is drawn at 64-80 logical pixels tall then nearest-neighbor enlarged; absolutely no soft airbrush, smooth vector curves, 3D rendering, painterly detail, glow gradients or photoreal texture.
Composition: square transparent PNG sprite sheet, exactly four frames in a regular 2 by 2 grid of equal cells. Each complete monster fully contained within its cell with at least 15% transparent margin. SAME character and scale in every frame, facing right and slightly toward viewer in an elevated three-quarter game view. All feet contact a consistent baseline. Reading order: 0 neutral battle stance; 1 alternate walking stance; 2 obvious attack anticipation, pulling head/body back and gathering energy; 3 fully extended attack toward RIGHT with a strong silhouette, open jaws or extended appendages appropriate to the species. Make frames 2 and 3 visibly different from neutral. NO baked-in long projectile, no broad impact or speed trails, no ground shadows; game engine adds these. Short species-specific energy at mouth/claws is okay only in frame 3. Transparent background with actual alpha, no text, labels, frame borders, scenic background, checkerboard or extra characters.
